metadata.title: Note on Interacting Langevin Diffusions: Gradient Structure and Ensemble Kalman Sampler by Garbuno-Inigo, Hoffmann, Li and Stuart

nodes.name: Theoretical behaviour of the interacting Langevin system at finite particle size
nodes.statement: The proposed formulation is primarily studied from a formal mean-field limit perspective, while the theoretical behaviour under a finite particle size is left as an open problem.
nodes.statement_short: Prior work analyses only the mean-field limit; finite-$J$ behaviour is unresolved.
nodes.section: Abstract

nodes.name: Interacting Langevin particle system
nodes.statement: \dot{u}^{(j)} = -C(U)\nabla \Psi_R(u^{(j)}) + \sqrt{2C(U)} \dot{\bf W}^{(j)},
nodes.statement_short: Particle SDE with covariance-preconditioned drift and multiplicative covariance noise.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Empirical covariance between particles $C(U)$
nodes.statement: The matrix $C(U)$ is chosen to be the empirical covariance between particles, \begin{equation} C(U) = \frac{1}{J} \sum_{k=1}^J (u^{(k)}-\bar{u})(u^{(k)}-\bar u)^{\rm T} \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Sample mean $\bar u$
nodes.statement: where $\bar u$ denotes the sample mean \begin{equation} \bar u = \frac{1}{J}\sum_{j=1}^J u^{(j)}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Full-rank requirement $J>d$
nodes.statement: We require $J>d$ in order for $C(U)$ to have full rank generically.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Validity for $J\le d$
nodes.statement: But we also note that (\ref{eq:IPS1}) is valid even for $J\le d$ in which case the dynamics is restricted to a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Macroscopic mean and covariance $m(\rho)$, $\mathcal{C}(\rho)$
nodes.statement: Here we have defined the macroscopic mean and covariance \begin{equation} m(\rho) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} u \rho(u) \,{\rm d}u, \qquad \mathcal{C}(\rho) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} (u-m(\rho))(u-m(\rho))^{\rm T} \rho(u)\, {\rm d}u \end{equation}

nodes.name: Product target measure $\pi(U)$
nodes.statement: the product measure \begin{equation} \pi(U) = \prod_{j=1}^J \pi^\ast(u^{(j)}) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Canonical measure $\pi^\ast$ associated with the potential $\Psi_R$
nodes.statement: Recall that $\pi^\ast(u)$ denotes the canonical measure associated with the potential $\Psi_R$, that is, $\pi^\ast(u) \propto \exp(-\Psi_R(u))$.

nodes.name: Compact form of the interacting particle system
nodes.statement: \dot{U} = S(U)\nabla \ln \pi(U) + \sqrt{2S(U)}\dot{\bf W},
nodes.statement_short: The $J$-particle system rewritten as a single $D$-dimensional preconditioned Langevin SDE.

nodes.name: Block diagonal preconditioner $S(U)$
nodes.statement: where $S(U) \in \mathbb{R}^{D\times D}$, $D = dJ$, is a block diagonal matrix with $J$ $d\times d$ entries $C(U)$ and ${\bf W}$ denotes standard $D$-dimensional Brownian motion.

nodes.statement: From \eqref{eq:FPE0} we see immediately that $\nabla \cdot (\pi \nabla \cdot S) = 0$ is a necessary condition for the invariance of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Per-particle divergence of the empirical covariance
nodes.statement: Using \begin{equation} C(U) = \frac{1}{J} \sum_{k=1}^M u^{(k)} (u^{(k)})^{\rm T} - \bar u \bar u^{\rm T}, \end{equation} an explicit calculation reveals then that \begin{align} \nabla_{u^{(j)}} \cdot C\,(U) &= \frac{d+1}{J} (u^{(j)} - \bar u)  \in \mathbb{R}^d \end{align}

nodes.name: One-dimensional Gaussian target: variance underestimation
nodes.statement: Let us consider a one-dimensional Gaussian target measure ($d=1$) with variance $b^2$, i.e. the potential is given by $\Psi_R(u) =  u^2/(2b^2)$. Under the approximating assumptions that the equilibrium density associated to \eqref{eq:IPS1} is a product of $J$ Gaussians with variance $\sigma^2$, and that the covariance at equilibrium can be well-approximated by the state-independent stationary covariance (mean-field assumption),  one can derive the  relation \begin{equation} \sigma^2 \approx \frac{J-2}{J} b^2, \end{equation} which we numerically verified for $J=4$. Note that $\sigma^2 < b^2$, i.e. the dynamics \eqref{eq:IPS1} systematically underestimates the posterior variance. Since $ \sigma^2 \xrightarrow{J \rightarrow \infty} b^2$, this error vanishes in the large-particle regime, in agreement with the results in \cite{sr:GIHLS19}.
nodes.statement_short: For a 1-D Gaussian target the uncorrected dynamics equilibrates at $\sigma^2\approx\frac{J-2}{J}b^2$, underestimating the variance for finite $J$.

nodes.statement:
The invariance of $\pi$ can be restored for the interacting Langevin diffusion model (ef{eq:IPS2}) if one replaces the drift term $S 
abla \ln \pi$ in (ef{eq:IPS2}) by $S

abla \Psi_R(u^{(j)}) +  rac{d+1}{J} (u^{(j)}- ar u) + \sqrt{2C(U)} \dot{ f W}^{(j)}, \end{equation} or, written more compactly  egin{equation} \dot{U} = S(U)
abla \ln \pi(U) +  rac{d+1}{J}(U- ar U) + \sqrt{2S(U)}\dot{ f W}, \end{equation} not only samples from the correct target density (ef{eq:TPDF}) but also gives rise to a gradient flow structure for the time evolution of the joint density $\mu$ over all particles at time $t \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Corrected interacting particle dynamics
nodes.statement: \dot{u}^{(j)} = -C(U)\nabla \Psi_R(u^{(j)}) + \frac{d+1}{J} (u^{(j)}-\bar u) + \sqrt{2C(U)} \dot{\bf W}^{(j)},

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (gradient flow structure of the corrected Fokker--Planck equation)
nodes.statement:
The Fokker--Planck equation associated to the time evolution of the joint density $\mu$ under the corrected interacting particle formulation (ef{eq:IPS2c})  is of the form  egin{equation} \partial_t \mu = 
abla \cdot \left( \mu\, S 
abla \left\{ \ln \mu  - \ln \pi ight\} ight) = 
abla \cdot \left( \mu \,S 
abla  rac{\delta V}{\delta \mu}ight), \end{equation} where the energy functional $V$ is the Kullback--Leibler divergence between $\mu$ and $\pi$, given by  egin{equation} V(\mu) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^D}  \mu(U) \{\ln \mu (U) - \ln \pi(U) \} \, {m d}U. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The corrected dynamics induces a Fokker--Planck equation that is a gradient flow of the KL divergence $V(\mu)$.
assumptions: The Fokker--Planck equation associated to the time evolution of the joint density $\mu$ under the corrected interacting particle formulation (\ref{eq:IPS2c})
conclusions: where the energy functional $V$ is the Kullback--Leibler divergence between $\mu$ and $\pi$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement:
Follows from the Fokker--Planck equation (ef{eq:FPE0}) for the SDE system (ef{eq:IPS2}), the substitution of the drift term $S 
abla \ln \pi$ by $S 
abla \ln \pi + 
abla \cdot S$, and Lemma ef{lemma1}. See, for example, \cite{sr:P14} for a derivation of the Fokker--Planck equation for SDEs with multiplicative noise, which leads to (ef{eq:FPE0}).
nodes.statement_short: Direct substitution: the added $\nabla\cdot S$ drift cancels the $\mu\nabla\cdot S$ term in the general Fokker--Planck equation, using Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Possible loss of positive definiteness of $C(U)$
nodes.statement: However, it cannot be guaranteed that $C(U)$ remains strictly positive definite for all times, in general, even under the condition $J>d$.
conclusions: it cannot be guaranteed that $C(U)$ remains strictly positive definite for all times

nodes.name: Regularised covariance $C_\alpha(U)$
nodes.statement: This suggests a regularisation of the form \begin{equation} C_{\alpha}(U) = \alpha C_0 + (1-\alpha)C(U), \end{equation} where $C_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ is a fixed symmetric strictly positive definite matrix and $\alpha \in (0,1)$ is a parameter.

nodes.name: Exponential convergence for the regularised finite-size system
nodes.statement: Under the Bakry--{\'E}mery condition \cite{sr:P14} stated in Proposition 2 of \cite{sr:GIHLS19} one can then also establish exponential convergence to the equilibrium measure for the finite-size particle system (\ref{eq:IPS1c}) with $C(U)$ replaced by $C_\alpha(U)$ and the correction term by $(1-\alpha) (d+1) (u^{(j)}-\bar u)/J$. This follows from standard arguments for the classical Fokker--Planck equation \cite{sr:P14}. See also Proposition 2 of \cite{sr:GIHLS19}.
nodes.statement_short: Under Bakry--Émery, the regularised corrected particle system converges exponentially to equilibrium.
assumptions: Under the Bakry--{\'E}mery condition \cite{sr:P14} stated in Proposition 2 of \cite{sr:GIHLS19}
with $C(U)$ replaced by $C_\alpha(U)$ and the correction term by $(1-\alpha) (d+1) (u^{(j)}-\bar u)/J$
conclusions: one can then also establish exponential convergence to the equilibrium measure for the finite-size particle system (\ref{eq:IPS1c})

nodes.name: Holley--Stroock relaxation of the convexity requirement
nodes.statement: Let us also mention that the convexity requirement on $\Psi_R$ can be relaxed by a perturbation argument due to Holley–-Stroock \cite{sr:P14}.

nodes.statement: The need for a correction term in (\ref{eq:IPS1}) can be avoided by ensuring that the $j$th block entry $C(U)$ in $S(U)$ does not depend on the $j$th particle position $u^{(j)}$. This can, for example, be achieved by defining the following modified covariance matrices
nodes.statement_short: Making the $j$th covariance block independent of $u^{(j)}$ removes the need for a correction term.
assumptions: by ensuring that the $j$th block entry $C(U)$ in $S(U)$ does not depend on the $j$th particle position $u^{(j)}$
conclusions: The need for a correction term in (\ref{eq:IPS1}) can be avoided

nodes.name: Modified (leave-one-out) covariance matrices $C_{[j]}(U)$
nodes.statement: This can, for example, be achieved by defining the following modified covariance matrices \begin{equation} C_{[j]}(U) = \frac{1}{J-1} \sum_{k\not=j} (u^{(k)}-\bar{u}_{[j]})(u^{(k)}-\bar u_{[j]})^{\rm T} \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}, \quad j=1,\ldots,J, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Properties of the finite-size particle system

nodes.name: Leave-one-out sample mean $\bar u_{[j]}$
nodes.statement: where $\bar u_{[j]}$ denotes the leave-one-out sample mean \begin{equation} \bar u_{[j]} = \frac{1}{J-1}\sum_{k\not=j}^J u^{(k)}, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Properties of the finite-size particle system

nodes.name: Correction-free interacting particle system with leave-one-out covariances
nodes.statement: \dot{u}^{(j)} = -C_{[j]}(U)\nabla \Psi_R(u^{(j)}) + \sqrt{2C_{[j]}(U)} \dot{\bf W}^{(j)}.
nodes.statement_short: Particle SDE using leave-one-out covariances, requiring no correction term.
nodes.section: 2 Properties of the finite-size particle system

nodes.name: Computational cost of the leave-one-out reformulation and link to EKS
nodes.statement: We note that very similar ideas have been employed, for example, in \cite{sr:LMW18} for second-order Langevin dynamics. However, while the reformulation (\ref{eq:IPS3}) is appealing, its computational implementation is more demanding due to the need for computing $J$ different covariance matrices and their square roots.  On the other hand, if the destabilising effect of the correction term in (\ref{eq:IPS1c}) leads to numerical difficulties under small or moderate particle sizes, then (\ref{eq:IPS3}) could be taken as a starting point for formulating gradient-free formulations in the spirit of the ensemble Kalman sampler (EKS) as proposed in \cite{sr:GIHLS19}.
nodes.statement_short: The leave-one-out variant costs $J$ covariance square roots but could seed gradient-free EKS-style formulations.
